The target `//third_party/web:minimist` that was mentioned in the exception looks like this:

```
ts_import(
    name = "minimist",
    srcs = [
        "@DefinitelyTyped//:minimist"
    ])
```

`ts_import` is a custom rule of ours:

```
ts_import = rule(
    implementation = _ts_import_impl,
    attrs = {
        "factory": attr.string(),
        "namespace": attr.string(),
        "replace": attr.string_dict(),
        "globals": attr.string_dict(),
        "deps": attr.label_list(),
        "undeclared_deps": attr.string_list(),
        "no_deps": attr.bool(),
        "srcs": attr.label_list(
            allow_files = FileType([".js", ".d.ts"]))
    },
    outputs = {
        "dts": "%{name}.d.ts",
        "js": "%{name}.js"
    })
```

`@DefinitelyTyped` looks like this:

```
    native.new_http_archive(
        name = "DefinitelyTyped",
        build_file_content = DEFINITELY_TYPED_BUILD_FILE,
        url = "[omitted]",
        sha256 = "[omitted]",
        strip_prefix = "[omitted]")
```

The `minimist` part of DefinitelyTyped's build file is:

```
filegroup(
    name = "minimist",
    srcs = [
        "minimist/minimist.d.ts"
    ])
```
@kchodorow could you take a look? This sounds like a potentially serious regression

Good news, I was able to create a small repro case!

* Download [crashdemo.zip](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/files/1020269/crashdemo.zip)
* The little shell script called `b` will run Bazel with the appropriate arguments. But to reproduce this bug, you need to use Bazel's remote caching feature, so you'll need set the environment variable `REST_CACHE_URL`. For example:

        REST_CACHE_URL=http://example.com/bazel-cache ./b

Two things:

1. It turns out this affects Bazel 0.4.5 as well.
2. The above commit to Asana/bazel was my own little workaround for the crash; I don't know if it is the correct fix.

This is actually related to remote caching, so I'm assigning to @ulfjack.

So, looks like there are several issues here.

The ArrayIndexOutOfBounds exception is most likely due to an action with 0 inputs. I fixed that at some point, but maybe I missed one code path. It's a known issue that passing bad host names will result in bad error messages / crashes for most of the remote caching implementations.
I can reproduce the original report. I was mistaken about having fixed this - I was thinking of another bug (but similar). The patch you have seems about right.

issue.title: Remote caching: don't crash for actions with no inputs
